title: Risk prioritisation and escalation
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, High risk work licence (reviewed 30 June 2026); SafeWork NSW, High risk work licences (last modified 15 June 2026; no visible date); WorkSafe Queensland, Boom type elevating work platform (WP) (no date shown).
audience: Property manager partner workers who find defects and must decide how urgently they are escalated
learningOutcomes: Rank defects by life safety, water ingress, security, service continuity and cosmetic impact.
Decide when to control access, stop work, or escalate to an authorised person.
Write an escalation that names the risk, the immediate protection and the owner of the next action.

instruction.heading: The priority order
instruction.body: Rank defects in this order: threats to life and to people's safety first, then water ingress and damage that spreads, then security of the property, then loss of essential services, and finally cosmetic defects. Within each band, consider how quickly the defect can get worse and who is affected. A defect can be urgent even when the cause is unknown. A ceiling panel that hangs over a corridor is urgent because of what could fall, whatever the reason it is loose.

instruction.heading: Control access before anything else
instruction.body: When a defect creates an immediate hazard, the first action is to control access. Keep people out of the affected area, mark it, and move occupants if necessary, in line with the site procedure. Do not attempt to fix the defect yourself if it needs a competent person, a licensed trade or specialist equipment. Summon the authorised person and record the time and the protection put in place.

instruction.heading: Write the escalation
instruction.body: An escalation states what was found, where, the risk, the protection put in place, the person who now owns the next action, and the date and time it was raised. Keep it factual. If the response is not received within the agreed period, escalate to the next person on the list and record that step. Do not promise a cause or a repair date that you have not established.

procedure: Rank the defect by life safety, water ingress, security, service continuity and cosmetic impact.
If there is an immediate hazard, control access and keep people clear of the area.
Do not attempt specialist repairs; summon the authorised person.
Write the escalation with the finding, location, risk, protection, next owner and time.
If no response is received within the agreed period, escalate to the next person and record it.
Keep the item open in the report until it is verified as resolved.

workedExamples.situation: A ceiling panel hangs loose over a busy corridor in a residential building.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first action, and what should the escalation say?
workedExamples.reasoning: The first action is to control access: close or mark the corridor section and keep people clear, in line with the site procedure. Summon the authorised specialist. The escalation states the location, the falling-object risk, the protection in place, the next owner and the time. It does not promise the cause or a repair date.

equipmentAndPpe: Barrier tape, cones or signage for access control
Escalation template with name, time and next owner
Phone or messaging for urgent contact

commonErrors.error: Treating a hazard as cosmetic because the cause is unknown.
commonErrors.prevention: Rank by what could happen. Control access first, then investigate.

commonErrors.error: Attempting a specialist repair to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Summon the authorised person and keep people clear.

commonErrors.error: Promising a cause or a repair date before diagnosis.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the risk and the next step only.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Work at height to inspect or repair an elevated defect is subject to “Ladders, elevated access and fall prevention”. A boom-type elevating work platform needs the WP licence in Victoria, with no boom-length threshold (WorkSafe Victoria page, reviewed 30 June 2026). In New South Wales and Queensland the licence applies at a boom of 11 metres or more, so a shorter boom may not need it there (SafeWork NSW licence page; WorkSafe Queensland page). This lesson does not grant a licence.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work, and escalation does not transfer any licence to the worker.

qualityStandard: Every defect is ranked in the agreed order with a stated reason.
An immediate hazard has access controlled before any other action.
Every escalation names the next owner and the time it was raised.
documentationEvidence: Risk ranking for each defect with the reason
Escalation record with time, recipient and next owner
Record of access control and protection put in place
summary: Rank by life safety first, then water, security, service and cosmetic impact.
Control access before anything else when a hazard is immediate.
Escalate with facts, the next owner and the time, and follow up if there is no response.

knowledgeChecks.question: A ceiling panel is loose over a busy corridor. What is the first action?
options: Remove the panel to see the cause, since the cause is needed before any control is set
Wait until the cause is known before taking any action on the corridor at all
Control access to the area and keep people clear, then summon the authorised person
Tell the manager the repair will be done tomorrow, so the corridor can stay open

knowledgeChecks.question: Which band ranks highest in the priority order?
options: Cosmetic defects on walls and doors
Loss of essential services at the site
Security of the property and contents
Threats to life and people's safety

knowledgeChecks.question: What does an escalation state, according to the lesson?
options: Only the name of the person to blame
What was found, where, the risk, the protection in place, the person who owns the next action, and the date and time raised
